chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Saif ibn 'Umeyra, from Mansur, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Ali (peace be upon him) was saying: 'When a son of al-mula'ana (the cursed mother) dies, and for him are brothers, his wealth would be upon the (legislated) shares of Allah.'

key_terms.ابْنُ الْمُلَاعَنَةِ: Son of the cursed mother (result of khul' or specific accusation procedure)

ai.seo_question: How is the estate of a son from the cursed mother (ibn al-mula'ana) distributed if he leaves behind brothers?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies that the son of 'al-mula'ana' is considered a full heir, as his estate is distributed among his brothers according to the standard Quranic shares (sahm Allah), rather than being treated as a stranger or having a unique ruling. This confirms the principle that the 'cursing' procedure affects the marital bond and legitimacy of the child but does not sever inheritance rights within the paternal lineage. The ruling underscores the stability of the paternal line in Shia jurisprudence, ensuring that the son inherits as a son of the father who underwent the 'ila' ceremony.
